propositions: Tests lack uniform per-test timeout budgets locally; 27 defects in two weeks were tests that could not fail or consumed excessive CI time due to absent subprocess return-code checks and missing timeout oracles.

Ruff lint configuration selects E, F, W, I, UP, B, BLE001, T201, SIM115, ASYNC, DTZ, RUF but excludes PLW1510 (336 findings, subprocess-run-without-check) and PT pytest-style codes (1811 findings, 481 of which are in the adopted subset), leaving 481 violations uncaught by make lint.

pytest-timeout 2.4.0 timeout, timeout_method, and timeout_func_only settings exist in pytest but are not configured in [tool.pytest.ini_options], only on CI command lines (--timeout=300 or higher), so local pytest runs have no budget.

Integration-tier tests like test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py consume 120–300 second subprocess ceilings (not observed durations) without explicit marks, creating uncertainty about whether lowering CI budgets to 20 s per test will cause timeouts.
Two hygiene check scripts (check_wall_clock_asserts.py, check_raw_git_writes.py) run in CI but are absent from make lint, fragmenting local verification from CI expectations.

CI workflow lanes for default and integration tiers carry inconsistent --timeout flags (300 or higher) that do not reflect the unit tier's actual 20 s budget, creating drift between local and CI timeout behavior.
